metadata.disclaimer: Based on NIST's crosswalk from CSF 2.0 to SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 (OLIR entry 186), with OSA's coverage estimates. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance or audit use.
metadata.clause_titles_from: NIST CSWP 29, The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0, as in NIST's Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool

crosswalk_check.source: NIST, CSF 2.0 to SP 800-53 Rev 5.2.0 crosswalk, v1.0.0 (OLIR entry 186, posted 2025-11-17)
crosswalk_check.scope: Base controls only, and every pair here is NIST's. The crosswalk names 719 pairs of a subcategory and a base control. One names RA-04, which SP 800-53 Rev 5 withdrew, and the other 718 are here. A row that names an enhancement, such as SA-11(02) for ID.RA-01, counts for its base control, as in the HIPAA and NERC CIP mappings. Russell agreed that rule on 2026-11-01. Such rows add 14 pairs, listed under from_enhancements_only, so the mapping has 732. None of the enhancements NIST names is withdrawn. OSA used no row that names a category or a whole control family in place of a subcategory and a control. On 1 November 2026 OSA dropped the 195 pairs of its own that it had kept beside NIST's, because their source can't be confirmed, and 2 of them came back from enhancement rows. added_from_source lists the 508 pairs OSA took from the crosswalk in October 2026, and OSA already had the other 210. The file fetched from NIST on 1 November 2026, as on 3 October, has a different checksum from the one NIST's catalogue lists for it, and both are given. The coverage figures, rationales and gaps are OSA's. coverage_review lists the ones one rater adjusted after the rebuild.

coverage_review.status: adjusted by one rater after the rebuild
coverage_review.method: In the rebuild of 1 November 2026, 88 clauses lost controls and 8 regained some from enhancement rows. One rater set the figure of each, against the SP 800-53 statements of the controls it now has and of the enhancements NIST names. Each rationale names only those controls. No figure is above OSA's earlier figure for the clause. A figure went down where the dropped controls carried part of the clause, and a clause with no control left has 0. Each changed figure ends its rationale with the reason, and the gaps say what is uncovered where they no longer matched the figure. Six raters shared the first pass, on the clauses that lost controls, by group of clauses. A seventh rater then re-rated the clauses that regained controls. Each figure was set by one rater.

clauses.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
clauses.rationale: PM-11 defines the organisation's mission and business processes with security and privacy risk in mind, and the protection needs that follow from them. Mission context is well addressed.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes organizational context beyond pure security mission alignment.

clauses.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered
clauses.rationale: SR-03, SR-05, SR-06 and SR-08 cover suppliers as stakeholders: supply chain processes, acquisition methods, supplier reviews and notification agreements. PM-30 sets the supply chain risk strategy and PM-09 the organisation-wide risk strategy. PM-18's privacy program plan reflects coordination among the teams responsible for privacy. OSA lowered this figure from 65% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for mission planning, critical infrastructure planning and contacts with security groups.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires systematic stakeholder identification and expectation analysis. SP 800-53 partially addresses through program-level controls.

clauses.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed
clauses.rationale: PM-01 covers compliance in the security program plan. Each family's policy control, from AC-01 to SR-01, requires policy consistent with applicable laws, regulations and other directives, including PT-01 for privacy. PM-28 records the constraints that shape risk decisions. OSA lowered this figure from 65% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for contractual requirements and rules of behaviour.
clauses.gaps: SP 800-53 lacks a dedicated legal/regulatory requirements identification control. Federal compliance assumed in FISMA context.

clauses.title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-08 covers the critical infrastructure plan, and PM-11 defines mission and business processes. RA-09 identifies critical system components and functions through a criticality analysis. CP-02, through its enhancement CP-02(08), identifies the critical assets that support essential functions. PM-30, through PM-30(01), identifies, prioritizes and assesses suppliers of critical items.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires explicit identification of stakeholder-dependent services. SP 800-53 addresses through mission/business process controls but less explicitly.

clauses.title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-11 defines the mission and business processes and the needs that follow from them. SA-09 sets requirements for external system services, and PM-30 and SR-05 set the strategy and methods for managing supply chain risk. OSA lowered this figure from 65% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for contingency planning and critical infrastructure dependencies.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes understanding dependencies on supply chain and partner services. SP 800-53 partially covers them through external service and supply chain controls.

clauses.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
clauses.rationale: PM-09 sets the organisation's risk management strategy, applies it across the organisation and keeps it current. RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance, and SR-02 plans for supply chain risk. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk framing and risk assessment policy.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for explicit risk management objectives that stakeholders agree. PM-09 sets them within the risk strategy, and agreement with stakeholders is left implicit.

clauses.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained
clauses.rationale: PM-09 sets the risk management strategy, which expresses the organisation's risk tolerance, and keeps it current. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk framing, which documents and shares risk tolerance.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for explicit risk appetite and risk tolerance statements. PM-09 expresses risk tolerance within the strategy and leaves risk appetite implicit.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes
clauses.rationale: PM-09 sets an organisation-wide strategy for security and privacy risk and applies it consistently. PM-03 brings security and privacy resources into capital planning. PM-30 and SR-02 add supply chain risk, and RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for enterprise risk framing and the security program plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes ERM integration. SP 800-53 supports but the integration with non-security enterprise risk is less explicit.

clauses.title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated
clauses.rationale: PM-09 sets the risk management strategy, including how the organisation mitigates risk. PM-28 records the assumptions, constraints, priorities and risk tolerance that shape risk responses. PM-30 and SR-02 set the strategy and plan for supply chain risk. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk assessment, risk response and remediation planning.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for clear direction on the options for responding to risk. PM-09 and PM-28 give that direction within the risk strategy and risk framing. The response options themselves are left to the organisation.

clauses.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties
clauses.rationale: PM-09 applies the risk management strategy across the organisation. PM-30 sets the supply chain risk strategy, including how it's communicated and who is responsible for it. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident reporting, threat sharing, security contacts and supply chain policy.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes lines of communication for cybersecurity risk across the organisation and with suppliers. The two strategies cover how risk is shared at a high level. Channels for reporting risks and incidents day to day are now uncovered.

clauses.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated
clauses.rationale: RA-03 assesses risk from threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact, and documents and shares the results. PM-09 names acceptable risk assessment methods in the strategy, and PM-28 records the assumptions, priorities and risk tolerance behind them. PM-30 and PM-18 extend the approach to supply chain and privacy risk. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk assessment policy and security categorisation.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for one standard method to calculate, record, categorise and prioritise risks. RA-03 covers a full risk assessment, and the categories used to group risks are left to the organisation.

clauses.title: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions
clauses.rationale: PM-09 risk management strategy may include opportunity considerations.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 explicitly addresses positive risks/opportunities. SP 800-53 is threat/vulnerability focused and does not address strategic opportunities.

clauses.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
clauses.rationale: PM-02, PM-19 and PM-29 appoint the senior officials accountable for security, privacy and risk management. PM-29 also sets up a risk executive function. PM-23 and PM-24 set up governance bodies for data. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security awareness, workforce development and the security program plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes leadership accountability and culture. These controls set leadership roles. Building a risk-aware, ethical culture is now uncovered.

clauses.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
clauses.rationale: PM-02, PM-19 and PM-29 appoint senior officials for security, privacy and risk management, with the authority and resources their roles need. PM-23 sets up a data governance body with defined roles and responsibilities. PM-13 runs a development program for the security and privacy workforce. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for position descriptions, position risk designation and the roles in personnel and planning policy.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for roles, responsibilities and authorities across the workforce, communicated and enforced. These controls cover senior roles and governance bodies. Roles for the rest of the workforce are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
clauses.rationale: PM-03 includes the resources the security and privacy programs need in capital planning and makes them available. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system-level resource allocation and workforce development.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 ties resource allocation to the risk strategy. PM-03 addresses resources, and allocation in proportion to risk is less explicit. Resource planning for each system is now uncovered.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
clauses.rationale: PS-01 sets personnel security policy and procedures. PS-09 writes security and privacy roles into position descriptions, and PS-07 sets security requirements for external personnel. PM-13 runs a development program for the security and privacy workforce. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for personnel screening, transfer and termination, access agreements, sanctions and security training.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for cybersecurity in every human resources practice, from hiring to departure. These controls set the policy and the roles. Screening, training, sanctions and the steps when people move or leave are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced
clauses.rationale: Each family's policy control, from AC-01 to SR-01, requires a policy and procedures that the organisation disseminates, reviews and updates. PM-01 sets the organisation-wide security program plan. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the risk management strategy and system security plans.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: SP 800-53 requires policy for each family and a comprehensive program plan. Well aligned with CSF policy requirements.

clauses.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission
clauses.rationale: Each family's policy control, from AC-01 to SR-01, requires the organisation to review and update its policy and procedures at set intervals and after set events. PM-01 reviews and updates the security program plan in the same way. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for continuous monitoring and remediation tracking.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes policy review driven by changes in threats and technology. The policy controls require review at set intervals and after set events. Monitoring results that would prompt an update are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
clauses.rationale: PM-09 reviews and updates the risk management strategy. PM-31 sets organisation-wide metrics, monitors them and reports the results, and RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance. PM-30 reviews the supply chain risk strategy in the same way.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes review of outcomes at strategy level. SP 800-53 covers it through organisation-wide monitoring metrics and strategy reviews, and explicit adjustment of the strategy is less formalized.

clauses.title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks
clauses.rationale: PM-09 reviews and updates the risk management strategy as the organisation changes, and PM-30 does the same for supply chain risk. PM-31 feeds the review with organisation-wide monitoring, and RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk framing, control assessments and risk assessment.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for a systematic review of whether the strategy covers the organisation's requirements and risks. PM-09 requires the strategy to be reviewed and updated, and a check of its coverage is less explicit.

clauses.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed
clauses.rationale: PM-06 develops, monitors and reports measures of security and privacy performance. PM-04 tracks the actions that respond to risk and reviews them against the risk strategy. RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance, and SR-06 reviews suppliers. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for control assessments, continuous monitoring and program testing.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for regular evaluation of how well cybersecurity risk management performs. PM-06 measures performance. Control assessments and ongoing monitoring are now uncovered.

clauses.title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
clauses.rationale: PM-30 sets an organisation-wide supply chain risk management strategy. SR-02 plans supply chain risk management for systems, and SR-03 sets the processes and controls that address supply chain weaknesses. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for supply chain risk management policy.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SP 800-53 Rev 5 SR family is well aligned with CSF supply chain governance.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
clauses.rationale: SR-02 plans supply chain risk management, including the roles and responsibilities that go with it. SR-03 runs supply chain processes in coordination with the people who have supply chain roles. SR-05 sets the acquisition strategies and contract tools that manage supply chain risk. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for supplier responsibilities in contracts, oversight of external services and supply chain policy.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 addresses the roles of customers and partners as well as suppliers. SP 800-53 focuses on supplier roles. Responsibilities written into supplier contracts and service agreements are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes
clauses.rationale: SR-01/SR-02 supply chain integration; PM-09 risk strategy integration; PM-30 supply chain risk management plan.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes integration with broader enterprise risk. SP 800-53 addresses supply chain risk management but enterprise-wide integration is less explicit.

clauses.title: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality
clauses.rationale: RA-09 identifies critical system components and functions, which shows the suppliers that matter most. SR-06 assesses and reviews the risks of each supplier, and SA-09 sets requirements for providers of external services. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for supply chain planning and processes, and acquisition contracts.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for suppliers to be known and ranked by criticality. RA-09 and SR-06 cover criticality and supplier reviews, and a list of suppliers ranked by criticality is left implicit.

clauses.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
clauses.rationale: SA-04 writes security and privacy requirements into acquisition contracts. SR-05 sets the acquisition strategies and contract tools that address supply chain risk, and SA-09 sets requirements for providers of external services. SR-03 and SR-06 cover supply chain processes and supplier reviews, and SR-10 inspects components for tampering. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for supply chain risk management policy and planning.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. SA-04 directly addresses contract requirements.

clauses.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
clauses.rationale: SR-05 sets acquisition strategies, contract tools and procurement methods that address supply chain risk. SR-06 assesses and reviews suppliers' risks, and SA-04 writes security requirements into acquisition contracts. SA-09 sets requirements for providers of external services.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes pre-engagement due diligence. SP 800-53 covers through acquisition and assessment controls.

clauses.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
clauses.rationale: SR-06 assesses and reviews supplier risks at set intervals, and SA-09 monitors external providers' compliance on an ongoing basis. SR-03 finds and addresses weaknesses in the supply chain. RA-09 shows which suppliers support critical components, and SA-04 sets requirements in contracts. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for risk assessment, risk response and supply chain planning.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 follows supplier risk through the whole relationship. SR-06 and SA-09 cover assessment and ongoing monitoring. Recording each supplier risk and choosing a response to it are less explicit.

clauses.title: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities
clauses.rationale: SR-08 sets agreements with supply chain entities for notice of compromises and assessment results. IR-01 and CP-01 set incident response and contingency policy. SA-04 and SA-09 carry security requirements into supplier contracts and service agreements, and SR-02 and SR-03 plan and run supply chain risk management. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident handling, the incident response plan and the contingency plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 brings suppliers into incident planning, response and recovery. SR-08 covers notification. The incident response and contingency plans, and suppliers' part in them, are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle
clauses.rationale: PM-30 sets the supply chain risk strategy, which can sit within the organisation-wide strategy PM-09 sets. SR-02 plans for supply chain risk across the life cycle of systems, from design to disposal, and SR-03 runs the supply chain processes and controls. PM-31 and SR-06 monitor performance and review suppliers.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes lifecycle monitoring of supply chain practices. SP 800-53 covers through supply chain and lifecycle controls.

clauses.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
clauses.rationale: SR-02 plans for supply chain risk across the life cycle, up to disposal. SA-04 and SA-09 set requirements in contracts and service agreements, and SR-05 sets the contract tools. SR-06 reviews suppliers' risks. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for component disposal and media sanitisation.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for plans covering what happens after a supplier relationship ends. SR-02 plans for disposal. Steps such as returning or destroying data and ending access are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained
clauses.rationale: CM-08 directly covers hardware component inventory with automated discovery; PM-05 system inventory.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained
clauses.rationale: CM-08 keeps an inventory of system components, including software, and PM-05 keeps the inventory of organisational systems. SA-09 and AC-20 cover external services and systems, and SA-05 keeps system documentation.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained
clauses.rationale: CA-03 documents information exchanges with other systems, and CA-09 documents internal system connections. PL-02 and PL-08 describe the system's connections and security architecture, and PM-07 places them in the enterprise architecture. AC-04 enforces approved information flows. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information location and boundary protection.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for maintained records of network communication and data flows. These controls document connections, exchanges and architecture, and a single data flow map is left implicit.

clauses.title: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained
clauses.rationale: SA-09 sets requirements and oversight for external system services, and AC-20 sets terms for using external systems. SR-02 plans supply chain risk management for the services the organisation acquires. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the system inventory and supplier reviews.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires specific supplier service inventory. SP 800-53 covers through external service controls but dedicated inventory less explicit.

clauses.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission
clauses.rationale: RA-02 categorises systems and information by the impact of their loss. RA-09 identifies critical components and functions, and RA-03 weighs the likelihood and harm of threats to them. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for mission process definition, contingency priorities and enterprise architecture.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 combines several criteria for setting asset priorities. SP 800-53 covers them through categorisation, criticality analysis and risk assessment, and ties to mission priorities are less explicit.

clauses.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained
clauses.rationale: CM-12 records where designated information is processed and stored, and who has access to it. CM-13 maps the actions the system performs on data. SI-12 manages and retains information as laws and requirements demand. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for security categorisation and the component inventory.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for inventories of designated data types and their metadata. CM-12 and CM-13 record where data sits and how it's processed, and an inventory of metadata is less formalized.

clauses.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles
clauses.rationale: SA-03 manages systems through a development life cycle, and SA-22 replaces components that are no longer supported. MA-02 and MA-06 cover maintenance, and SR-12 covers disposal of components. SI-12 manages and retains information through its life cycle.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 requires holistic lifecycle management. SP 800-53 covers through various lifecycle controls.

clauses.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-05 scans and monitors for vulnerabilities and analyses the results. SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories. CA-02, CA-07 and CA-08 find weaknesses through assessments, monitoring and penetration testing, and RA-03 records vulnerabilities in the risk assessment. SA-11, through its enhancement SA-11(02), and SA-15, through SA-15(07) and SA-15(08), have developers analyze threats and vulnerabilities during development.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
clauses.rationale: PM-16 threat awareness program; SI-05 security alerts; PM-15 security contacts.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-03 identifies threats and records them in the risk assessment. PM-16 runs a threat awareness program that shares threat intelligence, and PM-12 covers insider threats. SI-05 receives security alerts and advisories from outside sources.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded
clauses.rationale: RA-03 directly covers impact and likelihood assessment.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization
clauses.rationale: RA-03 combines threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood and impact to determine risk. RA-02 sets impact levels through categorisation, and PM-16 feeds in threat information. RA-07 responds to findings in line with the organisation's risk tolerance. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the risk strategy and plans of action and milestones.
clauses.gaps: Minimal: RA-07 strengthens coverage by formalizing risk response based on assessment findings.

clauses.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated
clauses.rationale: RA-07 responds to findings in line with the organisation's risk tolerance. PM-09 sets the strategy that guides the choice of response. PM-30 sets the supply chain risk strategy, and PM-18 the privacy program plan. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the risk assessment and plans of action and milestones.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for risk responses to be chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated. RA-07 and PM-09 cover the choice of response. Planning and tracking responses through plans of action and milestones are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked
clauses.rationale: CM-03 controls changes to the system and keeps records of them. CM-04 analyses each change for its security and privacy impact before it's made, and CA-07 monitors the system on an ongoing basis. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system authorisation and risk acceptance.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 covers exceptions as well as changes. CM-03 and CM-04 cover changes. Recording and tracking exceptions, such as accepted risks, are now uncovered.

clauses.title: Processes for receiving, analyzing, and responding to vulnerability disclosures are established
clauses.rationale: RA-05 scans for vulnerabilities, including newly reported ones. It analyses the results, fixes real vulnerabilities within set times and shares what it learns. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for flaw remediation, security advisories and contacts with security groups.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for a process to receive and act on vulnerability disclosures. RA-05 covers vulnerability management, and taking in reports from outside the organisation is less explicit. Security advisories from outside sources are now uncovered.

clauses.title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use
clauses.rationale: SR-11 keeps counterfeit components out, and SR-10 inspects components for tampering. SI-07 verifies the integrity of software, firmware and information. SR-05 and SA-04 set acquisition methods and contract requirements, and SA-10, SA-11 and SA-15 cover the developer's configuration management, testing and process.
clauses.gaps: Minor: SP 800-53 SR family covers hardware/software integrity comprehensively.

clauses.title: Critical suppliers are assessed prior to acquisition
clauses.rationale: SR-06 assesses and reviews the supply chain risks of suppliers and of what they provide, including their processes, ownership and own suppliers. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for acquisition methods, contract requirements and supply chain processes.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for critical suppliers to be assessed before acquisition. SR-06 covers supplier assessments at set intervals. Timing them before acquisition and focusing on critical suppliers are less explicit.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from evaluations
clauses.rationale: CA-02 assesses controls and reports the findings, and CA-05 turns them into plans of action and milestones. CA-07 monitors controls on an ongoing basis, and RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance. SA-17, through its enhancement SA-17(06), has developers structure security-relevant components so they can be tested.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes systematic improvement identification. SP 800-53 generates findings but improvement process less formalized.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties
clauses.rationale: CA-08 runs penetration tests, and IR-03 tests incident response. CP-04 tests the contingency plan and starts corrective action where needed. CA-05 turns weaknesses found into plans of action and milestones.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 includes third-party coordination in testing. SP 800-53 covers testing but supplier coordination less explicit.

clauses.title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities
clauses.rationale: IR-04 feeds lessons from incident handling back into procedures, training and testing. CP-02 and IR-08 update their plans after problems found in use. CA-07 and SI-04 monitor operations on an ongoing basis.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes improvements drawn from running operational processes. SP 800-53 draws them mainly from incidents, contingency events and monitoring, and other routine processes are less explicit.

clauses.title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved
clauses.rationale: IR-08 sets the incident response plan, and CP-02 sets the contingency plan. The organisation distributes, reviews and updates each plan after problems found in use or testing, and communicates the changes. PL-02 and SR-02 keep system security and supply chain plans current.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
clauses.rationale: IA-04 manages identifiers and IA-05 manages authenticators. AC-02 manages accounts. IA-02 and IA-08 identify and authenticate users inside and outside the organization, IA-03 does so for devices and IA-09 for services. IA-01 and AC-01 set the policies.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions
clauses.rationale: IA-12 proofs the identity of each user who needs an account. It resolves the identity to a unique individual and validates and verifies the identity evidence. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for managing identifiers and issuing authenticators.
clauses.gaps: Binding a proofed identity to its credentials when they are issued is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
clauses.rationale: IA-02 user authentication; IA-03 device authentication; IA-08 non-org users; IA-09 service identification.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified
clauses.rationale: IA-13 employs identity providers and authorization servers to manage identities and access rights. Its enhancements verify the source and integrity of identity assertions and access tokens, manage tokens and protect the keys that secure them. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for user authentication, authenticator management and session authenticity.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 addresses identity federation and assertion protocols. Protecting the session that carries an assertion is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
clauses.rationale: AC-02 account management; AC-03 access enforcement; AC-05 separation of duties; AC-06 least privilege; AC-24 access control decisions.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
clauses.rationale: PE-02 access authorizations; PE-03 access control; PE-06 monitoring; PE-08 access records.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
clauses.rationale: AT-02 gives all users literacy training and awareness, and AT-03 gives role-based training. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for training feedback and workforce development.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. Feedback on training results is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind
clauses.rationale: AT-03 gives role-based training to staff in the roles the organization names, before they get access and at set intervals after that. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident response training, workforce development and training feedback.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap. Feedback on training results, and a development program for the security workforce, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected
clauses.rationale: SC-28 protects the confidentiality and integrity of information at rest, with SC-12 managing keys and SC-13 providing cryptography. SI-07 detects unauthorized changes, and CP-09 backs up information for availability. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for media storage and transport, and access enforcement.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected
clauses.rationale: SC-08 protects the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information, with SC-12 managing keys and SC-13 providing cryptography. SC-07 protects boundaries, and SC-40 protects wireless links.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-use are protected
clauses.rationale: SC-04 information in shared resources; AC-03/AC-04 access and flow control; SC-39 process isolation.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 explicitly addresses data-in-use protection (confidential computing, memory protection). SP 800-53 covers through general controls but data-in-use is less explicitly addressed.

clauses.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested
clauses.rationale: CP-09 system backup; CP-06 alternate storage.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied
clauses.rationale: CM-01 to CM-11 cover configuration management. They set the policy, baselines and settings, control and analyze changes, restrict functions and software, and keep the component inventory and the configuration management plan.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
clauses.rationale: SI-02 finds and corrects flaws and installs security updates on time. CM-11 sets and enforces rules for software that users install, and SI-07 detects unauthorized changes to software. MA-03, through its enhancement MA-03(06), keeps the software on maintenance tools patched. SA-10, through SA-10(01), has developers make software and firmware integrity checkable. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for replacing unsupported components and removing unneeded functions.
clauses.gaps: Replacing software that is no longer supported, and removing software that isn't needed, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk
clauses.rationale: SC-49 enforces separation between security domains in hardware, and SC-51 write-protects firmware in hardware. CM-07, through its enhancement CM-07(09), keeps a list of authorized hardware and prohibits the rest. SA-10, through SA-10(03), has developers make hardware integrity checkable. SC-03 and SC-39, through SC-03(01) and SC-39(01), use hardware separation to isolate security functions and processes. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for hardware maintenance, replacing unsupported components and the component inventory.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for hardware to be maintained, replaced and removed in line with risk. Maintenance, the replacement of unsupported hardware and the component inventory are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
clauses.rationale: AU-02, AU-03 and AU-12 set the events to log and the content of each record, and generate the records. AU-06 and AU-07 review, analyze and report on them, and AU-11 keeps them. SA-15, through its enhancement SA-15(13), has developers log events in a set secure format.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented
clauses.rationale: CM-07, through its enhancements CM-07(02), CM-07(04) and CM-07(05), stops unauthorized programs from running, either by blocking listed software or by allowing only listed software. SC-34 loads the operating environment and chosen applications from hardware-enforced, read-only media on the components the organization picks. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for rules for user-installed software and signed components.
clauses.gaps: Rules for the software that users may install, and checks that components are signed, are uncovered here. CM-07 covers what may run.

clauses.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle
clauses.rationale: SA family comprehensive for secure development lifecycle.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage
clauses.rationale: SC-07 protects boundaries and separates subnetworks. AC-04 controls information flows, and AC-03 enforces access. SC-04 and SC-05 protect shared resources and availability. OSA lowered this figure from 95% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for remote access and system partitioning.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats
clauses.rationale: PE family comprehensive for environmental protection.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
clauses.rationale: SC-36 distributes processing and storage across locations or domains, and SC-06 protects resource availability. SI-13 swaps in standby components before predictable failures, and SC-24 fails to a known state. SA-08 and SA-24 build resilience into system design, and SC-39 isolates processes. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for contingency planning, alternate sites, backup and recovery.
clauses.gaps: Alternate processing sites, backup and recovery after an outage are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained
clauses.rationale: CP-06 and CP-07 provide alternate storage and processing sites, and CP-08 provides alternate telecommunications services. They give spare capacity when the primary site fails. PM-03 plans the resources the security program needs, and PM-09 sets the risk management strategy. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for capacity planning, log storage capacity, denial-of-service protection and emergency power.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 addresses general capacity management. Monitoring and planning the capacity of systems in day-to-day use is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
clauses.rationale: SI-04 monitors systems and networks, and SC-07 monitors communications at boundaries. CA-07 runs continuous monitoring, and AU-12 generates audit records.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events
clauses.rationale: PE-06 monitoring physical access; PE-03 physical access control; PE-20 asset monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
clauses.rationale: AU-12 generates audit records, and AC-02 monitors the use of accounts. AU-13 watches open sources for disclosure of information. CM-10 and CM-11 govern how software is used and installed, and CA-07 runs continuous monitoring. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for audit record review and system monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Reviewing and analyzing audit records for unusual activity is uncovered here.

clauses.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
clauses.rationale: SA-09 monitors control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis. PS-07 monitors providers' compliance with personnel security requirements. CA-07 and SI-04 add continuous and system monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses external service monitoring. SP 800-53 covers through general monitoring and service controls.

clauses.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events
clauses.rationale: SI-04 monitors systems, and SI-07 detects unauthorized changes to software, firmware and information. CM-03 controls configuration changes, and AU-12 generates audit records. SC-35 seeks out malicious code on the network.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities
clauses.rationale: SI-04 system monitoring; AU-06 audit analysis; IR-04 incident handling/analysis.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Information is correlated from multiple sources
clauses.rationale: AU-06 analyzes audit records, and its enhancements correlate records across repositories and integrate their analysis with other sources. SI-04 monitors systems, and one of its enhancements correlates monitoring information. CA-07 correlates and analyzes the results of assessments and monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The estimated impact and scope of adverse events are understood
clauses.rationale: PM-11 defines mission and business processes and the protection they need. PM-28 records risk priorities and risk tolerance. PM-09, PM-18 and PM-30 set the risk management, privacy and supply chain risk strategies. Together they give the context for judging an event's impact. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident analysis, risk assessment, audit review and system monitoring.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 asks for the impact and scope of each adverse event to be estimated as it is analyzed. The controls here set the context at program level. Estimating the impact of each event is uncovered.

clauses.title: Information on adverse events is provided to authorized staff and tools
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, including detection and analysis. PM-16 shares threat intelligence across the organization, and PM-15 shares threat and incident information with outside security groups. RA-10 hunts for threats that evade other controls. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for monitoring alerts, incident reporting and audit review.
clauses.gaps: Alerts from monitoring tools to staff and to incident response tools, and the reporting of incidents, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis
clauses.rationale: PM-16 runs a threat awareness program that shares threat intelligence. RA-10 hunts for threats, and RA-03 assesses risk from the threats and vulnerabilities it identifies. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for receiving security alerts and advisories.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes threat intelligence integration into analysis. SP 800-53 covers threat intelligence and says less about using it in analysis. Receiving security alerts and advisories from outside sources is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, including detection and analysis. IR-08 sets the incident response plan, which defines reportable incidents.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
clauses.rationale: IR-08 sets the incident response plan and names who is responsible for incident response. IR-07 provides incident response support, and IR-06 reports incidents to the authorities the organization names. SR-08 sets notification agreements with suppliers, and SR-03 works on supply chain weaknesses with supply chain staff. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident handling.
clauses.gaps: Handling each incident under the plan is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling includes triage; IR-05 incident monitoring.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Incidents are categorized and prioritized
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling includes categorization; IR-05 monitoring for tracking.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 emphasizes formal categorization and prioritization. SP 800-53 IR controls cover but with less categorization specificity.

clauses.title: Incidents are escalated or elevated as needed
clauses.rationale: IR-04 incident handling; IR-06 reporting (includes escalation); IR-07 assistance.
clauses.gaps: Minor: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses escalation procedures. SP 800-53 covers through incident reporting.

clauses.title: The criteria for initiating incident recovery are applied
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling from preparation through to recovery. IR-08 sets the incident response plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires specific recovery initiation criteria. SP 800-53 covers recovery but formal criteria less explicit.

clauses.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, including the analysis of each incident. AU-07 reduces audit records and generates reports for after-the-fact investigations. SI-02, through its enhancement SI-02(07) on root cause analysis, finds the underlying causes of issues or failures and acts on them.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Actions performed during an investigation are recorded, and the records' integrity and provenance are preserved
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, and IR-06 reports incidents. AU-07 supports after-the-fact investigations and leaves the original content and time order of audit records unaltered. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for protecting and retaining audit records.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes the integrity of investigation records and their chain of custody. Protecting those records from change, and keeping them, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, and IR-06 reports incidents. AU-07 draws reports from audit records for investigations and leaves their original content and time order unaltered. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for audit record content, protection and retention.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 is more specific than SP 800-53 on metadata and provenance. Recording the content of audit records, and protecting and keeping them, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: An incident's magnitude is estimated and validated
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, including analysis. RA-03 determines the likelihood and magnitude of harm, and RA-07 responds to findings in line with risk tolerance. IR-08 sets the incident response plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses magnitude estimation. SP 800-53 covers through incident analysis.

clauses.title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
clauses.rationale: IR-06 incident reporting; IR-07 incident response assistance and coordination.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Information is shared with designated internal and external stakeholders
clauses.rationale: IR-06 reports incidents to the authorities the organization names. SR-08 sets notification agreements with suppliers, and SR-03 works with supply chain staff. IR-04 handles incidents, and IR-07 helps users handle and report them. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for information sharing with security groups and the threat awareness program.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes structured incident information sharing. Sharing incident information with peer groups and information sharing organizations is uncovered here.

clauses.title: Incidents are contained
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, which includes containment. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for isolating systems at network boundaries.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Incidents are eradicated
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling, which includes eradication. OSA lowered this figure from 90% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for removing malicious code.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
clauses.rationale: CP-10 recovers and reconstitutes systems to a known state. IR-04 handles incidents through to recovery, and IR-08 sets the incident response plan.
clauses.gaps: Minimal gap.

clauses.title: Recovery actions are selected, scoped, prioritized, and performed
clauses.rationale: CP-10 recovers and reconstitutes systems to a known state within the recovery time and recovery point objectives. IR-04 handles incidents through to recovery, and IR-08 sets the incident response plan. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for the contingency plan's recovery objectives and restoration priorities.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes business impact in setting recovery priorities. Setting recovery objectives and restoration priorities in a contingency plan is uncovered here.

clauses.title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
clauses.rationale: CP-09 backs up information and protects the integrity of backups, and its first enhancement tests backups for reliability and integrity. CP-04 tests the contingency plan, and CP-02 sets it. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for integrity checks on software, firmware and information.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 explicitly requires integrity verification before restoration. CP-09's first enhancement covers testing backups. Integrity checks on other restoration assets, such as software images and firmware, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: Critical mission functions and cybersecurity risk management are considered to establish post-incident operational norms
clauses.rationale: PM-11 defines mission and business processes, PM-08 plans for critical infrastructure, and PM-09 sets the risk management strategy. IR-01 and IR-08 set the incident response policy and plan. OSA lowered this figure from 75% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for system recovery and incident handling.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 addresses establishment of new operational norms post-incident. SP 800-53 covers recovery but post-incident norm establishment less explicit.

clauses.title: The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed
clauses.rationale: CP-10 recovers and reconstitutes the system to a known state after a disruption, compromise or failure. OSA lowered this figure from 85% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for integrity verification and continuous monitoring.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes verifying integrity after recovery. Checking the integrity of restored assets, and confirming normal operation by monitoring, are uncovered here.

clauses.title: The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed
clauses.rationale: IR-04 sets up incident handling and feeds lessons learned back into procedures, training and testing. IR-08 sets the incident response plan.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 requires formal recovery closure criteria. SP 800-53 covers incident closure but formal end-of-recovery criteria less explicit.

clauses.title: Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
clauses.rationale: IR-06 reports incident information to the authorities the organization names. SR-08 sets notification agreements with suppliers, and IR-04 handles incidents through to recovery. OSA lowered this figure from 80% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for sharing contingency information and incident response assistance.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 emphasizes recovery-specific communication. SP 800-53 covers through incident reporting but recovery communication specifically is less detailed.

clauses.title: Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging
clauses.rationale: CP-02 sets the contingency plan, including how contingency information is shared. IR-04 handles incidents through to recovery. OSA lowered this figure from 70% on 1 November 2026, when it dropped its earlier controls for incident reporting and incident response assistance.
clauses.gaps: CSF 2.0 specifically addresses public communications. Approving and sharing public updates on recovery is uncovered here.
